title: The Home Rule Leagues, 1916

endcard.line: Pictures: unknown photographer (public domain); Falk Studio, Sydney (public domain)

segments.say: In nineteen sixteen, India got not one Home Rule League, but two.
Bal Gangadhar Tilak, back from prison in Mandalay, founded the first in April, at Belgaum. Annie Besant founded the second in September, at Adyar in Madras.
Besant had backed Ireland's own Home Rule movement, and brought its idea to India.

anim.title: What they wanted
items: Dominion status, like Canada or Australia

segments.say: Their demand was self-government within the British Empire, the kind of dominion status that Canada and Australia already had.

items.text: Britain names responsible government as its goal
the League becomes the Swarajya Sabha

segments.say: The movement pushed Britain to concede that responsible government in India was its final aim. In nineteen twenty, the league was renamed the Swarajya Sabha.

anim.title: Why it mattered
items: Ground prepared for the mass movements that followed

segments.say: With Congress split and the war on, the leagues kept the demand for self-rule alive, and set the stage for the movements that followed.
For GS One, remember: two leagues in nineteen sixteen, Tilak's and Besant's, asking for self-rule within the Empire.

sources: PIB, PM's remarks on Lokmanya Tilak commemorative coins, 23 July 2007 (relid 29341): the Home Rule Movement that Tilak started with Annie Besant forced the British to concede that introduction of responsible government was their final objective
PIB, Heroes of Indian Freedom Struggle (Independence Day 2018 page): in 1916 Besant launched the All India Home Rule League along with Lokmanya Tilak

Wikipedia, 'All India Home Rule League' (read): Tilak founded the first league at Belgaum in April 1916; Besant founded the second at Adyar, Madras, in September 1916; Besant a supporter of the Irish Home Rule movement; Tilak had been imprisoned in Mandalay; split in the Congress; movement set the stage for the independence movement; renamed Swarajya Sabha in 1920
Wikipedia, 'Home rule' (read): in 1916 nationalist leaders demanded self-government and dominion status within the British Empire as enjoyed by Australia, Canada and others

quiz.q: Where did Tilak found his Home Rule League in April 1916?
quiz.why: Tilak at Belgaum (April); Besant at Adyar, Madras (September).

quiz.q: What did the Home Rule Leagues demand?
quiz.why: Self-government on the lines of the dominions.

quiz.q: What was the All India Home Rule League renamed in 1920?
quiz.why: It became the Swarajya Sabha in 1920.

reviewNote: Tilak and Besant are long dead and shown only in period portraits. The joint launch and the 'responsible government' outcome are from PIB; the dates, places and 1920 renaming are from Wikipedia, which also calls the movement Besant-led; check the dates against NCERT Class 12 'Themes in Indian History III' or the National Archives before approval. The script doesn't name the August 1917 declaration's author, because no official text was read. Moving facts: none.
